fn abs_val(x: Int) -> Int
  requires true
  ensures result >= 0 and (result == x or result == -x)
  effects pure
  example abs_val(5) == 5
  example abs_val(-5) == 5
  example abs_val(0) == 0
{
  if x >= 0 then x else -x
}

def abs_val(x: int) -> int:
    return x if x >= 0 else -x

fn clamp(x: Int, lo: Int, hi: Int) -> Int
  requires lo <= hi
  ensures result >= lo and result <= hi
  ensures (x < lo and result == lo) or (x > hi and result == hi) or (x >= lo and x <= hi and result == x)
  effects pure
  example clamp(5, 1, 10) == 5
  example clamp(-5, 1, 10) == 1
  example clamp(15, 1, 10) == 10
  example clamp(1, 1, 10) == 1
  example clamp(10, 1, 10) == 10
  example clamp(3, 3, 3) == 3
{
  if x < lo then lo else if x > hi then hi else x
}

fn clamp(x: Int, lo: Int, hi: Int) -> Int
  requires lo <= hi
  ensures result >= lo and result <= hi and ((x < lo and result == lo) or (x > hi and result == hi) or (x >= lo and x <= hi and result == x))
  effects pure
  example clamp(5, 1, 10) == 5
  example clamp(-5, 1, 10) == 1
  example clamp(15, 1, 10) == 10
  example clamp(1, 1, 10) == 1
  example clamp(10, 1, 10) == 10
  example clamp(3, 3, 3) == 3
{
  if x < lo then lo else if x > hi then hi else x
}

fn contains(xs: List[Int], x: Int) -> Bool
  requires true
  ensures true
  effects pure
  example contains([], 1) == false
  example contains([1, 2, 3], 2) == true
  example contains([1, 2, 3], 4) == false
  example contains([5], 5) == true
{
  match xs {
    [] => false
    [h, ..t] => if h == x then true else contains(t, x)
  }
}

fn factorial(n: Int) -> Int
  requires n >= 0
  ensures result >= 1
  effects pure
  example factorial(0) == 1
  example factorial(1) == 1
  example factorial(5) == 120
  example factorial(10) == 3628800
{
  if n == 0 then 1 else n * factorial(n - 1)
}

fn gcd(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
  requires a >= 0 and b >= 0 and (a > 0 or b > 0)
  ensures result > 0 and a % result == 0 and b % result == 0
  effects pure
  example gcd(12, 8) == 4
  example gcd(0, 5) == 5
  example gcd(7, 0) == 7
  example gcd(1, 1) == 1
  example gcd(48, 18) == 6
{
  if b == 0 then a else gcd(b, a % b)
}

fn max_of(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
  requires true
  ensures result >= a and result >= b and (result == a or result == b)
  effects pure
  example max_of(1, 2) == 2
  example max_of(5, 5) == 5
  example max_of(-3, -7) == -3
  example max_of(0, 0) == 0
{
  if a >= b then a else b
}

def max_of(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return a if a >= b else b

fn reverse_helper(xs: List[Int], acc: List[Int]) -> List[Int]
  requires true
  ensures true
  effects pure
  example reverse_helper([], []) == []
  example reverse_helper([1, 2, 3], []) == [3, 2, 1]
{
  match xs {
    [] => acc
    [h, ..t] => reverse_helper(t, [h] ++ acc)
  }
}

fn reverse_list(xs: List[Int]) -> List[Int]
  requires true
  ensures true
  effects pure
  example reverse_list([]) == []
  example reverse_list([1, 2, 3]) == [3, 2, 1]
  example reverse_list([42]) == [42]
{
  reverse_helper(xs, [])
}

def reverse_list(xs: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    return xs[::-1]

fn safe_div(a: Int, b: Int) -> Option[Int]
  requires true
  ensures (b == 0 and result == None) or (b != 0 and result == Some(a / b))
  effects pure
  example safe_div(10, 2) == Some(5)
  example safe_div(7, 2) == Some(3)
  example safe_div(-7, 2) == Some(-4)
  example safe_div(5, 0) == None
{
  if b == 0 then None else Some(a / b)
}

fn sum_list(xs: List[Int]) -> Int
  requires true
  ensures (xs == [] and result == 0) or (xs != [] and true)
  effects pure
  example sum_list([]) == 0
  example sum_list([1, 2, 3]) == 6
  example sum_list([5]) == 5
  example sum_list([-1, 1]) == 0
{
  match xs {
    [] => 0
    [h, ..t] => h + sum_list(t)
  }
}
